purpose: Meaning layer for Tesseract: what traditional motifs are documented or believed to mean, with an evidence grade for every claim. Feeds meaning-to-form selection; never used to copy motifs.

evidenceLevels.folk-name: The pattern's vernacular name is recorded (e.g. in Selivachov's lexicon of folk pattern names). The strongest evidence of how makers themselves saw it.
evidenceLevels.folklore: The motif's plant or animal carries this meaning in documented folk songs, rites or customs (wedding songs, carols).
evidenceLevels.ethnographic: Use in a documented context (wedding, funeral, protective garment) is recorded by ethnographers; the meaning is inferred from that use.
evidenceLevels.period-emblem: The meaning is documented in period emblem or symbol literature (e.g. Renaissance emblem books).
evidenceLevels.scholarly-interpretive: Proposed by scholars from comparative or archaeological study; plausible but not attested by the makers.
evidenceLevels.popular-modern: Widely repeated in modern popular sources; origin and age unclear.
evidenceLevels.contested: Scholars consider the meaning a modern construction or disputed.
evidenceLevels.none-documented: No reliable symbolic meaning recorded; the motif is decorative or functional.

policy: Tesseract states meanings only at their evidence grade; unknown meanings stay unknown (v3 non-negotiable).
Meanings guide the choice and arrangement of ASCEND's own primitives; traditional motifs themselves are never copied.
Native American traditions: structure only. No motif semantics are recorded or used for commercial derivation; nation-specific and sacred material is excluded.

Archaism note (Nykorak et al. 2022): geometric sash motifs are probably the oldest layer and began as protective signs, but most lost their meaning and became decorative; only folk names keep the associations. So a folk name is evidence of how makers saw the shape, not proof of an ancient meaning.

structure.form: rhombus, often subdivided into four with a dot in each part; chains of rhombs in bands

regions: widespread; dense geometric forms in Podillia, Bukovyna, Hutsul region

meanings.claim: sown field, fertility of earth and people
meanings.note: Very widely repeated; the 'sown field' reading is also argued in archaeological literature (Trypillia-era rhomb-and-dot signs).

meanings.claim: worn on wedding garments and by expectant mothers as a wish for a good harvest or a healthy child

structure.form: vertical axis with symmetric branches, often a vase or ground at the base and birds above; central motif on rushnyk ends

regions: Central and Northern Ukraine rushnyky (Kyiv region, Poltava, Chernihiv)

meanings.claim: links underworld, earth and heaven; continuity of generations
central motif of wedding and ritual rushnyky

motifs.caution: v3 anti-generic rule: never as an automatic tree-of-life composition. Use the axis-and-branch structure, not the stock image.

structure.form: branch with clustered round berries and leaves, red and black

meanings.claim: girlhood, love, beauty, motherhood, continuity of family; homeland
meanings.note: Kalyna is one of the most frequent symbols in Ukrainian folk song.

structure.form: climbing vine with curling tendrils and cone-like fruit

meanings.claim: youth, vitality, fertility; marriage
meanings.note: Hops appear in wedding songs and rites.

structure.form: vine with leaves and bunches, often a continuous border

meanings.claim: family, household, abundance
meanings.note: The grapevine ('виноград') is a recurrent image in carols (koliadky) and wedding songs.

structure.form: lobed leaves, often on men's shirts

meanings.claim: strength, endurance, manhood

structure.form: rosette with rotational symmetry (often D4 or D8)

meanings.claim: the name 'ruzha' is a recorded folk name for rosette motifs
sun, light, beauty
'рожа' / 'ружа' / 'ружки' name the 8-petal rosette typical of West Ukrainian pick-up sashes; 8- and 6-petal rosettes are read by the authors as solar signs
meanings.note: The solar reading is the authors' interpretation (scholarly-interpretive); the name is folk.

structure.form: two overlaid squares or rhombs, D8 symmetry

meanings.claim: sun, cosmic order, protection
stars on sashes are called 'зірниці', 'звізди', 'штерна'

structure.form: paired spirals curling outward from a centre (mirror pair)

meanings.claim: the name 'ram's horns' is a recorded folk name of the motif
prosperity, strength
in West Ukrainian sashes the hooked rhomb is called 'баранячі ріжки'; Lithuanian weavers call the same shape 'жабка' (little frog)
meanings.note: Selivachov p. 277, cited in the article. One shape, two folk readings: names are local, not universal.

structure.form: continuous interlocking hook or meander line, usually a band

meanings.claim: the name 'bezkonechnyk' (the endless one) is a recorded folk name
eternity, continuity of life

structure.form: zigzag or wave line in bands

meanings.claim: 'kryvulka' is a recorded folk name
water, road, life path
'кривульки' recorded on West Ukrainian sashes alongside 'очка', 'розквітлий хрест', 'розклиння'

structure.form: paired birds facing a tree or axis (mirror pair)

meanings.claim: paired birds as bride and groom, in wedding contexts
birds as souls or messengers; spring

structure.form: frontal figure with raised arms, often flanked by riders or birds; northern rushnyky

meanings.claim: the motif itself is documented on rushnyky
a protective mother-goddess named 'Berehynia'
meanings.note: The national 'Berehynia' goddess reading is widely regarded as a late-20th-century construction.

meanings.claim: the female figure, the vase (flowerpot / tree) and the double-headed eagle on 19th-century Dnipro-region rushnyky are iconographically and stylistically related variants of one composition
meanings.note: Plate caption in Selivachov's Lexicon, p. 53: 'Іконографічна та стилістична спорідненість зображень богині, вазона та двоголового орла у вишиваних рушниках XIX ст. Подніпров'я'.

structure.form: geometric figure in women's shirts of Podillia

meanings.claim: a reading of geometric Podillia shirt ornament as a deer-goddess image

structure.form: palette

meanings.claim: red: life, love, protection; black: earth
palettes are strongly regional (e.g. Poltava white-on-white, Hutsul multicolour)

structure.form: central rhomb with horn-like side figures; chains of rhombs ('showers') on rushnyki

meanings.claim: sown field or sun; fertility and protection
chains of rhombs read as rain

structure.form: mirrored bird pair on rushnyk

meanings.claim: duck and drake as bride and groom; family life

structure.form: palette

meanings.claim: predominantly red threads on white linen
red as life, sun, health

names.en: Jacobean crewelwork tree of life (17th c.)

structure.form: sinuous tree on a hillock with exotic leaves and flowers, wool crewel on linen-cotton twill

meanings.claim: the style draws on Indian painted cottons (palampores) brought by the East India trade
meanings.note: Documented trade and design history rather than a symbolic meaning.

names.en: Elizabethan and Stuart emblem flowers and blackwork (16th–17th c.)

structure.form: scrolling coiling stems enclosing single flowers (strawberry, pansy, honeysuckle, pea pod); counted-thread blackwork fillings

meanings.claim: flowers carried emblem meanings (e.g. pansy: thoughts/remembrance) recorded in period emblem literature
blackwork fillings: decorative geometric filling patterns

structure.form: horizontal bands of repeating border patterns, alphabets, verses, figures

meanings.claim: a record of stitches and patterns and a demonstration of skill and education
border patterns themselves

structure.form: tight scrolling stems, wild-rose flowers and leaves, tooled and bevelled in leather

meanings.claim: regional saddlery craft style; no fixed symbolic meaning

structure.form: multiple parallel rows of decorative stitching forming scrolls, flames or florals on shaft panels

meanings.claim: stitch rows stiffen the shaft and decorate it

structure.form: five-pointed star inlay or stitching

meanings.claim: Texan identity

names.en: beadwork, quillwork, weaving and other traditions of specific nations

structure.form: learned only as abstract structure: band rhythm, symmetry group, density

motifs.policy: No motif semantics are recorded or used. Nation-specific, ceremonial and sacred designs are excluded from derivation (v3).

structure.form: row of nested angles (chevrons) along the band; frieze p1m1 or p11g/p2mg when alternating

regions: West Ukraine sashes; Lithuania (the oldest Lithuanian plant motif)

meanings.claim: named after the fir tree in both Ukraine and Lithuania
evergreen life, tree-of-life kinship

structure.form: four rhombs in a block, or one rhomb split into four; rhomb with inscribed figure (D4)

meanings.claim: 'віконця', 'вічка', 'скриньки' are recorded folk names (Selivachov p. 191)
rhomb figures of this kind read as solar signs

structure.form: voluminous square with three dots; repeat 8–12 cm along the sash

regions: Pokuttia, West Podillia; typically green on red

meanings.claim: 'павучки' is the recorded folk name of the pattern

structure.form: six triangles arranged in a circle (C6/D6 rosette)

meanings.claim: 'сонечко' is the recorded folk name
sun
meanings.note: Here the name itself carries the meaning.

structure.form: a closed band around the body: the wrap-around band itself

meanings.claim: protective (apotropaic): 'takes into a circle', separates the wearer from the outside world; close in symbolism to the wreath
meanings.note: Belief held in the Carpathians until the mid-20th c.; red sash protected the groom from the evil eye in Polissia (early 20th c.).

meanings.claim: status and age of the wearer; going to church or visiting unbelted was unacceptable
life passages: red sash over a baby's swaddling before christening, kept until the child's wedding as a pledge of a happy marriage; wedding binding; coffin lowered on sashes (Lithuania)
in Lithuania the sash plays the gift and ritual role the rushnyk plays in Ukraine; today given for birthdays, graduation, university entry as a wish of success

motifs.useInAscend: Direct support for ASCEND's cuff, collar and belt bands: a closed band = protection by enclosure. The wrap-around rule (no motif cut at the seam) also keeps the circle unbroken.

structure.form: elongated and hooked rhombs; group of five rhombs

meanings.claim: recorded Lithuanian folk names: 'рожа' for an elongated rhomb, 'жабка' for a hooked rhomb, 'свічки' for five rhombs

structure.form: S-shaped hooks on diagonal axes; dynamic rhythm (rotation, not mirror: frieze p2 / p11g)

meanings.claim: 'вужі' (grass snakes) is the recorded folk name
the grass snake is a household guardian in Lithuanian folklore
meanings.note: Well attested in Lithuanian folklore generally; not stated in this article. Upgrade with Tumėnas 2002.

structure.form: four-arm cross with bent arms; C4 rotation without mirror

meanings.claim: pre-20th-century folk sun sign on Lithuanian sashes

motifs.useInAscend: Structure only (C4 rotation without mirror). Never generate a hooked-cross form: in Western markets it reads as the Nazi symbol whatever its folk origin.

structure.form: every motif along the sash is different (no repeat); grid of small rhomb-based cells

meanings.claim: a showpiece of the weaver's skill: no two motifs alike

motifs.useInAscend: Precedent for a band where every cell differs: exactly the capacity a secure-glyph data skeleton needs (each cell a symbol). Lithuanian sashes also carried woven text (songs, and today standard inscriptions).

rules: symmetric about the vertical axis and short horizontal axes; measured, static rhythm
1-, 3-, 5- or 7-part symmetric layout across the width: widest, richest band in the centre; narrower bands with finer motifs on each side; framed by thin stripes
'здвоєні' ornaments: half-motifs in neighbouring bands meet to form a whole
alternation of rhomb and oblique cross; lattices of rhombs with inscribed motifs
colour 'shimmer': close hues within one motif; no fixed dominant figure/ground contrast
two-faced weaves: positive and negative sides of the same pattern
Pokuttia: horizontal bands at the ends, tripartite division
men's sashes 10–18 cm wide, women's 8–12 cm, 1.5–2 m long; 'павучки' repeat 8–12 cm
diagonal axes; dynamic S-motifs and hooked crosses
fragmentary motifs cut off by the band edge
dark ornament on a light ground; sharp contrast
'stouzorni': every motif different; woven text (songs, inscriptions)
